title: Mind Your Bias: A Critical Review of Bias Detection Methods for Contextual Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring associations between gendered names/terms and attributes (e.g., career/family, occupations) using WEAT-derivative methods (s-SEAT, w-SEAT, CEAT) via cosine similarity of contextualized embeddings and masked language model probabilities (LPBS).

Evaluating associations between European American and African American names/terms and attributes (e.g., pleasantness) using contextualized embedding cosine similarities and log probability bias scores.
Measuring associations between recommended/non-recommended phrases for disabilities and positive/negative traits using cosine similarity-based metrics and masked language model predictions.

Testing emergent and intersectional stereotypes (e.g., comparing European American males vs. African American females) against intersectional attributes using contextualized embedding similarities and probability-based scores.
Comparing associations of mental versus physical diseases with temporary or permanent attributes using WEAT-based contextualized embedding methods.
Used as a baseline validation test to measure expected associations (e.g., flowers vs. insects and pleasantness) using cosine similarity of embeddings and word prediction probabilities.
